memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Israelites are to observe the Sabbath, celebrating it for the generations to come as a lasting covenant. It will be a sign between me and the Israelites forever, for in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed." - Exodus 31:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God grounds the Sabbath in creation itself. He rested on the seventh day, and He calls that rest a pattern for His people. The rhythm of work and rest is not a later religious invention; it is woven into the fabric of the world from the beginning.

Notice the word used of God: "rested and was refreshed." God was not tired — He does not grow weary (Isa 40:28). The language is deliberate and warm, describing not exhaustion but satisfied enjoyment. God stopped, looked at what He had made, and delighted in it. Rest, at its heart, is about enjoying rather than merely recovering.

That reframes rest for us. It is not simply collapsing because we are depleted. It is stopping to enjoy — enjoying God, enjoying what He has given, enjoying the people around us, enjoying being rather than producing. Many of us have never learned this. We only stop when we break. God invites something better: a regular, deliberate ceasing in which we look at our life and give thanks rather than push harder.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is my rest merely collapsing from exhaustion, or genuine enjoyment and gratitude?
What has God given me that I have not stopped long enough to enjoy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You rested and were refreshed, delighting in what You had made. Teach me to rest not only from exhaustion but with enjoyment and gratitude for all You have given. Amen.
